citation.authors: Lew KK, Ho KK, Keng SB, Ho KH
citation.title: Soft-tissue cephalometric norms in Chinese adults with esthetic facial profiles

secondHand.via: Moate & Darendeliler 2002, Tables IV and VI

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08: norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 30 differences (logs/task9a2-compare-<id>.log). Every mean and SD of both extractors re-read from the page images (PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24), and the settled file checked by script against a third, independent reading of the pages (the table in sets.test.ts). Decisions: (0) Source text normalised to one pattern giving table, page, row and column with sex and age (a and b worded it differently; prose only). Adult band: a [18, 40] / b none -> [18, 40] (P18 note; 'adults', text p. 22). (1) Upper lip strain 14 mm (a: #79 'different', M and F) not entered; Table VI strain 1.5 ± 1.5 kept close (merge notes); fix round 1 (8 Oct): -> different, not used (owner LIP-1). (2) 'Upper lip mm' 15 (a and b: #89, M and F) not entered: decided from the page, see caveat (Table VI gives no length; 15 is Lew's basic upper lip thickness). (3) Table VI 'Upper lip thickness' 15.0 ± 1.5: a and b both #78 -> #77 basic upper lip thickness (Holdaway's list order and value; see the definitionNote). A curation call by the implementer, flagged for review. (4) Nasolabial 95 a same / b close -> close (method not in the compilation, merge notes). Page images: PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24 (Tables I-VI), rendered at 2000 px. Owner LIP-3 (8 Oct, after LIP-2 flipped the catalogue's #79 to Holdaway's direction): upper lip strain different -> close, used.

caveats: Quoted second-hand from Moate & Darendeliler 2002 (Aust Orthod J 18:19-26, a compilation of published Chinese cephalometric norms), Tables IV and VI; the original paper was not read. The compilation rounds every mean and SD to whole numbers (Lew's soft tissue to 0.5) and gives no landmark, plane or method definitions.
The compilation states no film scale or magnification for any study; assumed true size (owner ruling M-2).
48 Chinese adults with aesthetic profiles (text p. 22). Region Singapore per the task brief (the compilation does not name the place). No age range or sex split is given.

Table IV heads this column 'Lew10', but reference 10 is Jacobson 1975; the column was identified by the author name against Moate's reference list (Lew et al. 1992 is reference 11), as both extractors did.
Table VI has no reference mark; the text attributes it to Lew, Ho and Keng (p. 22). Its values are pooled (no sex split); its Caucasian column is not entered.

Not entered: upper lip strain 14 mm (Table IV row 20, males and females; Table V row 13 'Lip Strain' 14). 14 mm is implausible as a strain and contradicts Lew's own Table VI strain, 1.5 ± 1.5 mm. It matches Holdaway's lip thickness at the vermilion (13-14 mm), so it may be that measurement mislabelled; not entered as either (merge notes).

Not entered: Upper lip 15 mm (Table IV row 19 'Upper lip mm', males and females), which Table V row 12 relabels 'Upper lip length'. Lew's own Table VI gives no lip length; it gives 'Upper lip thickness 15.0 ± 1.5' (entered as #77). An upper lip length (subnasale to stomion, #89) of 15 mm would be short for an adult, so the 15 is read as the same basic thickness repeated without its SD. Catalogue #89, added from these tables (owner M5), therefore gets no norm from this compilation (raised with the owner).

Upper lip strain, Table VI 1.5 ± 1.5 mm: used, close (owner ruling LIP-3, 8 Oct, replacing LIP-1's 'kept but not used'), after the catalogue's #79 was flipped to Holdaway's direction (LIP-2). Caution: Moate gives Lew's strain as 14 mm in Table IV and 1.5 ± 1.5 in Table VI; the 1.5 matches Holdaway's convention and Moate's Caucasian column.
Not in the catalogue: upper lip curvature (Table VI, 5.5 ± 1.5 mm).
Table V (p. 24) repeats the nasolabial, lip and strain values; not entered separately.

Entered as Holdaway's basic upper lip thickness (#77), not the thickness at the vermilion (#78): Lew's Table VI lists Holdaway's eleven soft-tissue measurements in Holdaway's order, and this row sits where Holdaway's 'basic upper lip thickness' sits (after skeletal convexity, before upper lip strain); its 15.0 mm is Holdaway's basic thickness (15 mm; his vermilion thickness is 13–14 mm, AlBarakati 2012 Table 3), and the compilation's Caucasian column prints the same 15.0; method not in the compilation (Lew 1992 quoted second-hand).
